title: K-flat tensor models for inverse image under a coefficient extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ and uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Work on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For $W=X,Y$ put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$, $B_{F,W,m}=(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m)_W$ for $F=E,L$ and $m\geq1$, with quotient projections $\pi^F_{W,m}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Write $G_F=g^{-1}$ on completed-coefficient module complexes, transporting the action along the ring isomorphism $c_F:g^{-1}\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}\simeq\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,X}$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. These maps satisfy $\pi^F_{X,m}c_F=c^g_{\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m}g^{-1}(\pi^F_{Y,m})$. Tensor products below are sheaf tensor products and their total complexes [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

For every flat-term K-flat complex $P$ of $R_Y$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], the complex $G_EP$ is flat-term K-flat over $R_X$. The complexes $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$ and $Z=G_EP\otimes_{R_X}S_X$ are flat-term K-flat over $S_Y$ and $S_X$, respectively. There is a natural isomorphism of complexes of $S_X$-modules
$$b_P:Z\xrightarrow{\sim}G_LQ,$$
with local formula
$$b_P(y\otimes s)=g^{-1}(p\otimes s_0),\qquad y=g^{-1}p,\quad s=c_L(g^{-1}s_0).$$
For every $m$, the square of complexes whose horizontal maps are $b_P$ and the analogous finite-coefficient tensor comparison
$$G_E(P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{E,Y,m})\otimes_{B_{E,X,m}}B_{L,X,m}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_L(P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{L,Y,m})$$
and whose vertical maps are the coefficient quotient maps commutes; on the upper left the quotient map is $G_EP\otimes_{R_X}S_X\to G_E(P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{E,Y,m})\otimes_{B_{E,X,m}}B_{L,X,m}$. The $G_E$ notation here means the underlying inverse image with its finite coefficient action transported by $c^g_{\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m}$. The finite comparisons commute with the quotient transitions, using the same-index maps $\iota_m:\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m\to\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m$ of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension].

On the ordinary unbounded derived categories of completed-coefficient modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], set $C_WH=H\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$. For a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$, $Z$ represents $C_XG_EK$, $Q$ represents $C_YK$, and $[b_P]$ represents a natural isomorphism $b_K:C_XG_EK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_LC_YK$, independent of the resolution under the canonical K-flat comparisons. No derived completeness or constructibility of $K$ is required.

proof.text:
Write $j_W:R_W\to S_W$ for the coefficient map, characterized by $\pi^L_{W,m}j_W=(\iota_m)_W\pi^E_{W,m}$. The maps $\iota_m$ and their transition compatibility are supplied by [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]; the limit and its coordinate projections are those of [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. We first check $c_Lg^{-1}(j_Y)=j_Xc_E$. After composing with $\pi^L_{X,m}$, the left side is
$$c^g_{A_{L,m}}g^{-1}((\iota_m)_Y)g^{-1}(\pi^E_{Y,m})=(\iota_m)_Xc^g_{A_{E,m}}g^{-1}(\pi^E_{Y,m})=(\iota_m)_X\pi^E_{X,m}c_E,$$
which is the $m$-th projection of the right side. The first equality is naturality in the coefficient ring of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](3), and the second is the defining projection equation for $c_E$ in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Equality of all coordinate maps into the limit proves the assertion. The same naturality also gives $(\iota_m)_Xc^g_{A_{E,m}}=c^g_{A_{L,m}}g^{-1}((\iota_m)_Y)$.

proof.text: Regard $(g^{-1},c_E)$ as a morphism of ringed topoi from $(X_{\mathrm{proet}},R_X)$ to $(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},R_Y)$. Its module pullback is $g^{-1}P\otimes_{g^{-1}R_Y}R_X$, canonically $G_EP$ since $c_E$ is invertible [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Apply the flat-term K-flat preservation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to $P$. It gives that $G_EP$ is K-flat with flat terms. Apply [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] to $R_Y\to S_Y$ and $P$, and to $R_X\to S_X$ and $G_EP$. It gives precisely that $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$ and $Z=G_EP\otimes_{R_X}S_X$ are K-flat with flat terms over $S_Y$ and $S_X$. No flatness of either coefficient map is a hypothesis of these cited statements.

proof.text:
In each degree apply the change-of-rings clause of [lem-pur-isomorphism-inverse-image-tensor-hom] to the ring sheaf $R_Y$, its algebra $S_Y$, and $P^n$. Its inverse tensor comparison, after transporting the two rings by $c_E,c_L$, gives
$$b_P:G_EP\otimes_{R_X}S_X\xrightarrow{\sim}G_L(P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y).$$
The coefficient identity in Step 1 identifies the balancing actions, so these transported tensor products are over exactly $R_X$ and $S_X$. On local sections the comparison is $g^{-1}p\otimes c_L(g^{-1}s_0)\mapsto g^{-1}(p\otimes s_0)$, by the local formula of the cited tensor comparison. In particular it is $S_X$-linear. Naturality in $P^n$ makes these maps commute with $d_P^n$ and with every chain map $P\to P'$. The coefficient complex $S_Y$ is concentrated in degree zero, so the total-complex differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is just $d_P\otimes1$. Thus the degreewise isomorphisms form the stated natural isomorphism of complexes.

proof.text:
Fix $m$ and abbreviate $B_{F,W,m}$ to $B_{F,W}$ and $c^g_{A_{F,m}}$ to $c_{F,m}$. The same tensor comparison, with the coefficient projections in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], identifies $G_E(P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{E,Y})$ with $G_EP\otimes_{R_X}B_{E,X}$. Reassociate after extension along $(\iota_m)_X$ by the mutually inverse maps
$$(y\otimes a)\otimes t\mapsto y\otimes\iota_m(a)t,\qquad y\otimes t\mapsto(y\otimes1)\otimes t.$$
They respect the balancing relations because $R_X\to B_{L,X}$ factors through $B_{E,X}$ by Step 1. Consequently the finite comparison $b_{P,m}$ has formula
$$g^{-1}(p\otimes a)\otimes t\longmapsto g^{-1}\bigl(p\otimes(\iota_m)_Y(a)c_{L,m}^{-1}(t)\bigr).$$
Here and below inverse images of local scalars are understood. Its inverse sends $g^{-1}(p\otimes u)$ to $g^{-1}(p\otimes1)\otimes c_{L,m}(g^{-1}u)$. The two composites are identities by balancing and the finite coefficient identity of Step 1. These formulas define maps of sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]: they respect restrictions and balanced additivity before sheafification. They commute with $d_P\otimes1$, giving the required finite isomorphism of complexes.

source.place: Tags 03EK (section-tensor-product) and 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback); explicit balanced reassociation and finite coefficient calculation.

proof.text:
For $y=g^{-1}p$ and $s=c_L(g^{-1}s_0)$ the upper-left vertical map is
$$y\otimes s\longmapsto g^{-1}(p\otimes1)\otimes\pi^L_{X,m}(s).$$
Step 4 then sends it to $g^{-1}(p\otimes\pi^L_{Y,m}(s_0))$, using $\pi^L_{X,m}c_L=c_{L,m}g^{-1}(\pi^L_{Y,m})$ from [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Applying $b_P$ first and the upper-right quotient map second gives the same expression. Local tensors generate the presheaf tensor product and hence determine maps out of its sheafification [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], so the square commutes. For transitions let $q_F:B_{F,W,m+1}\to B_{F,W,m}$. Starting with $g^{-1}(p\otimes a)\otimes t$ at level $m+1$, both paths give
$$g^{-1}\bigl(p\otimes\iota_m(q_Ea)c_{L,m}^{-1}(q_Lt)\bigr).$$
Indeed $q_L\iota_{m+1}=\iota_mq_E$ by [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and $q_Lc_{L,m+1}=c_{L,m}g^{-1}(q_L)$ by [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](3). This proves transition compatibility also when the extension is ramified; the inclusion $\varpi_E^m\mathcal O_L\subset\varpi_L^m\mathcal O_L$ used to define $\iota_m$ is sufficient.

proof.text: Let $K$ be any complex representing the given derived object. Choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The completed-coefficient inverse-image module functor is exact and preserves quasi-isomorphisms by the Structure isomorphism paragraph of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Hence $G_EP\to G_EK$ is a quasi-isomorphism and, by Step 2, a flat-term K-flat resolution. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](2), $Q$ represents $C_YK$ and $Z$ represents $C_XG_EK$. The exact functor $G_L$ carries the representative $Q$ to a representative of $G_LC_YK$. Localizing the complex isomorphism $b_P$ therefore gives an isomorphism $b_K:C_XG_EK\to G_LC_YK$. The cited resolution and derived change-of-rings results are unbounded and have no derived-completeness or constructibility assumption.

proof.text:
For a chain map $a:P\to P'$ between flat-term K-flat complexes the generator formula of Step 3 gives the strict equation
$$b_{P'}(G_Ea\otimes1)=G_L(a\otimes1)b_P.$$
These additive termwise functors carry a chain homotopy $h$ to $G_Eh\otimes1$ and $G_L(h\otimes1)$, respectively; the identity $a-a'=dh+hd$ is preserved. Thus the equation is natural on the homotopy category. For a quasi-isomorphism $a$ both vertical maps become invertible: $G_Ea$ is a quasi-isomorphism by exactness [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], its endpoints are K-flat by Step 2, and coefficient extension preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](1); the same applies to $a$ followed by the exact $G_L$. The equivalence $W_{R_Y}^{-1}\mathcal P_{R_Y}\simeq D(R_Y)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] now descends this natural isomorphism. Explicitly, naturality for an inverted quasi-isomorphism follows by multiplying the displayed equality by its two invertible images, and then for every composite of ordinary maps and inverted quasi-isomorphisms. The descended component is the $[b_P]$ of Step 6. Applying the same equality to the canonical comparison between any two K-flat representatives shows that these components agree under the canonical representative identifications of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings](2). This proves naturality in $K$ and independence of the resolution.
